theMerge.resolutionsJudged: Three prose files conflicted and I read each as a judgement rather than a mechanical merge. skills/legion-architect/SKILL.md and its bundle: main reworded the acceptance sentence and dropped 'and, for a parent, that every child is done (section 3)'; the resolution keeps main's wording and carries this branch's --paginate onto it. That drop is main's deliberate change and not a loss - the same main text describes SIGNOFF_CHILD_IN_WORKFLOW and the park_child alternative, and the daemon refuses the acceptance for an open descendant before any move to retro, so the prose duty was replaced by a refusal rather than forgotten, and a reader is nowhere told a parent may be accepted while a child still runs. docs/site concepts.md: both sides survive whole, this branch's merging row saying GitHub completes the merge under the base branch's own rules and main's awaiting_merge row keeping the merged-root exception. Neither merged text tells a reader anything false.
theMerge.deletionSurvival: Main brought 11,632 added lines across 179 files in this merge, which is the largest surface a deleted claim could have returned from. Swept at this head: no instruction anywhere to write, fill, cite or update a pull request body CI line; the retired phrases only inside prompts_test.go's own list; no surviving sentence asserting READY reads a head's checks or required set, the one loose grep hit in architect-common.md being a false positive across two unrelated sentences of one long line, checked and discarded; the absolute no-CI claim absent; no conflict marker in the tree.

whatIVerifiedMyself: Both fingerprints at my own two heads, and then the per-file attribution at both normalisations rather than accepting either count.
The three resolutions read against both parents, and the dropped parent-children clause checked against the daemon refusal that now carries it rather than assumed deliberate.
The deletion-survival sweep over the merged tree, including the one false-positive hit resolved rather than left as a maybe.

I read the required checks of the code commit on GitHub myself before approving and carry no verdict or run id forward as what the head holds now: the required set is lint, typecheck, test and pr-title with no branch-protection checks, every required name's newest run at the code commit had completed and succeeded when I read it, nothing there was failed, cancelled or timed out, the only lane still running was the non-required dispatch check, and the compare from that commit to the head I approve returned handoffsOnly true over two files.
notBlockingButNamed: The implementer's evidence and the pull request body give the fingerprint account as --context 0 while reporting the five-path result and the hashes that belong to the default-context run. I measured both: the documented recipe gives two paths, the default context gives five, and every path of both is accounted for, so no conclusion moves and nothing is hidden - but the command named and the numbers reported come from different runs, which is the shape this issue exists to remove and the reason I state both accounts here, so the record carries the right pairing whether or not the body is rewritten. Retro's body pass is where it belongs rather than a round: the canonical values the branch must act on are the tester's and are correct, and a reader who runs the stated command reaches the stated conclusion by a different count.
